1 big thing: Battle of the bots
 
Illustration: Aïda Amer/Axios. Stock: Getty Images

Axios' Ina Fried recently tested two of the newest personal AI agents, OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse.

  • Ina writes: I asked each assistant to plan a trip to Atlanta to see my beloved WNBA Golden State Valkyries, organize a brunch watch party and create souvenir programs.

☀️ Where they shined: When I asked both agents to find flights and tickets for Game 3 in Atlanta, each caught that the game had been moved up a day and that tickets weren't yet on sale.

  • Both found good flight options.

🧐 Where they were creative, but imperfect: For my brunch, Muse designed a colorful 10-page recipe booklet featuring ube waffles and lavender-honey butter.

  • Dots produced a more practical eight-page packet with detailed cooking instructions and attention to dietary preferences.
  • Both designed invitations that needed aesthetic and language edits.

👎 Where they struggled: I asked the agents to help me buy Valkyries trading cards.

  • Both helped me compare options and prices. I chose Target, where I had a 5% discount and free shipping.

Muse tried to complete the purchase, but got stuck at Target's sign-in page.

  • Dots directed me to the Target app, where my account and payment information were already saved.

💵 The bottom line: Both agents could have done more if I gave them greater access to my accounts and wallet — but I don't trust them enough for that yet.

2. 🚀 Cancer meds in space
 
The exhaust plume of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket is seen this morning from Winter Haven, Fla. Photo: Joe Skipper/Reuters

Orbital pharma startup Varda Space Industries launched a mission today to test microgravity's effects on an innovative cancer treatment, Alex Fitzpatrick reports.

  • Developing medicine in space, away from the pesky influence of Earth's gravity, could unlock better treatments — though commercial scale for "space meds" is still a moonshot.
Varda's W-1 vehicle after landing in 2024. Photo: John Kraus/Varda

🛰️ The California company's W-7 spacecraft launched into orbit from Cape Canaveral, Florida, on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rideshare mission.

  • Varda is testing whether the key ingredient in next-gen cancer medicines called PROTACs will crystallize differently in microgravity than it does on Earth — possibly making the treatment easier for recipients' bodies to absorb.
  • For missions like this one, the company can create "seed quantities" in space, then return the results to Earth to be propagated, Varda chief strategy officer Michael Reilly tells Axios.

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
People clear debris after an air attack in Kyiv yesterday. Photo: Oleksii Filippov/AFP via Getty Images
  1. 🇺🇦 Secretary of State Marco Rubio told Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in a phone call today that President Trump hasn't issued any kind of order to harm Ukraine. The call was an effort to push back on Ukrainian accusations that Trump is trying to coerce Zelensky into making concessions to Russia. More from Barak Ravid.
  2. 👨‍💼 Axios exclusive: Joel Kaplan, Meta's chief global affairs officer, will leave Meta next year after 15+ years as Mark Zuckerberg's top Washington adviser. Zuckerberg tells Axios: "Joel has worked on virtually every tough issue Meta has faced for more than 15 years." Go deeper.
  3. 💰 Thieves stole nearly $1 million worth of trading cards last week from a FedEx truck parked for 60-90 minutes outside a Professional Sports Authenticator grading center in Santa Ana, Calif., The Athletic reports. PSA had "graded" the cards for the owners, verifying authenticity and condition. High grades boost cards' resale value. Gift link.
 
 
4. 🏀 1 sports thing: NBA tips off
 
Cover: Mark Ulriksen for The New Yorker

"Make It Two," by artist Mark Ulriksen, is the cover of this week's issue of The New Yorker. The painting shows the joyous starting lineup of the New York Knicks, last season's champions.

The 2026-27 NBA season tipped off this afternoon, with the Boston Celtics visiting the Detroit Pistons starting at 3 p.m. ET.

  • ESPN's ball-knowers favor the Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs.

🏆 Knicks fans, still riding high on last year's historic championship run, are hoping for a repeat. That hasn't happened since the Golden State Warriors did it in 2017 and 2018.
